text.p: Kuwaiti authorities have released five Iraqi fishermen who were seized by Kuwait's coastal guards in February, newspapers said on Monday.
They said the fishermen were abducted by Kuwait's coastal guards on February 22 while they were inside Iraq's territorial waters close to Mina al-Bakr and al-Amiya port.
The papers did not say when the fishermen were freed.

"They were subjected to arbitary measures during their detention...They were taken with their hands tied to state security offices in Kuwait city where they were tortured and charged with espionage for Iraq," they said.
The newspapers, quoting an Iraqi News Agency reporter in the area, said Kuwaiti coastal guards had seized the fishermen within the demilitarized zone.
They gave the names of the five fishermen and their ages.
"The Kuwaiti coastal guards brandished weapons which are banned to be carried within the zone," they said.
They said Kuwaiti coastal guards continued molesting Iraqi fishermen, violating Iraqi territorial waters with their gunboats.
